chapter: N'goma drums and the scrapbook clippings
title: His song lyrics, No Parkin' Today
summary: Kline reads the lyrics of an undated song Morehouse wrote about parking in Forest Hills.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: This is undated. Apparently Chauncey was writing a song when he was living in Forest Hills. It's written on his letterhead, 68-31 Ingram Street, Forest Hills, 75. Some of the notes and some of the lyrics are here. I'll read the lyrics. It's entitled 'No Parkin' Today.' "No matter where I drive my car today, when my gal and I have pretty things to say, the traffic problem is awful, even down around Jamaica Bay. There is a man in a blue suit standing there, no parkin' today. Drive on to Sheepshead Bay, to Lundy's for a bite, oh I'm playing it low because my pocketbook is light. The parkin' lot attendant, a man of enormous height, says if you ain't goin' to eat, just don't sit in that seat. No parkin' today."
